calls.title: ASAPP + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The meeting revolved around improving the current experiment analysis workflow, which is facing challenges due to its piecemeal nature, limiting scalability. The team discussed GrowthBook's capabilities, including its unified feature flagging and experimentation platform that supports both cloud and self-hosted options, catering to enterprise needs for data privacy and compliance. Key features highlighted were the structured experiment templates, role-based access controls, and meta-analysis dashboards, which collectively enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of experiments. The discussion also covered the upcoming Proof of Concept (POC) to validate the integration with data warehouses and ensure ease of use for diverse teams. Additionally, GrowthBook's simple pricing model and the emphasis on fostering a culture of continuous learning through experiment analysis were noteworthy points.
calls.keywords: experimentation, self-hosting, data warehouse, POC, feature flags, meta-analysis

Communication channels via Slack were confirmed, ensuring rapid troubleshooting support as the team navigates through the adoption of new tools.

calls.summary:
# ASAPP + GrowthBook
Date: 2026-11-17 | Duration: 35.279998779296875m

## Summary
The production A/B experiment was scaled to 100% and concluded successfully, with a winning variant selected after testing an additional option. A slight decline in one quality metric was accepted because latency and cost improved, while the open-source platform continued to support configuration, metrics, and analysis needs. Several experiments are planned, with adoption expected across four or five teams during the next two quarters. Governance remains under development, especially metric ownership, new-metric requests, and trade-off decisions. Experiment configurations are maintained in GitHub, while GrowthBook’s UI is mainly used for analysis and reporting. GrowthBook may eventually replace Unleash for allocation, but migration would require changes across many services. The current $200,000 enterprise fee was viewed as high compared with nearly $40,000 in annual Unleash costs. Christian will prepare a more reasonable pricing proposal, and Julian will review it.

## Keywords
GrowthBook, A/B testing, Experiment allocation, MCP server, Multi-armed bandits, Unleash migration
